text:
Alex: Quick follow-up on the cross-lang SDK connection window + retry UX. We need to pick sensible defaults before the RFC merge so downstreams don't get surprised.

Priya: I think we should default to a small client-side window (1-2 in-flight pages) and prefer explicit pagination for heavy list workloads. Keeps memory and headroom predictable. :thumbsup:

Marco: Agree on a small window but we need a graceful resume story for streaming. If we push an opaque resume token to the client, languages without native async iterators (Go) can still resume cleanly when they rehydrate.

Sara: Important callout: retries must be idempotent at the operation level, not the page. If retrying a page can return overlapping items, clients need to dedupe by stable id. We should document this clearly.

Alex: +1. Rough mapping idea: transport modes = "unary-paged" (explicit next_token), "stream-resume" (streaming chunks + resume token), "stream-idempotent" (server guarantees ordered non-overlap). Default SDK mapping: TS -> streaming-first, Python -> streaming-first with synchronous iterator fallback, Go -> paged-first with streaming helper.

Priya: For backoff, expose a config object `RetryPolicy { maxRetries, baseMs, maxMs, jitter }` and allow per-route overrides. That avoids surprising global behavior for enterprise routes.

Marco: We also must clarify cancellation semantics. When a consumer cancels an iterator, the SDK should attempt a polite shutdown (send a connection-level abandon), but the server must accept cancellation and free resources quickly. Otherwise clients will leak sockets.

Alex: Edge-case: paged fetch + partial progress + retry budget exhaustion. Idea: keep a per-session retry budget tied to the client session rather than per-page. That prevents a flaky page from burning infinite retries across the whole session.

Sara: That matches production complaints: SDKs that retried every page aggressively inflate backend load. Per-session budget prevents cascading retries.

Priya: Implementation sketch (TS):
```
const session = sdk.session({ retryBudget: 5 })
for await (const page of session.listItems()) {
  // consume page
}
if (session.error?.name === 'RetryBudgetExceeded') {
  // surface friendly error to caller
}
```
When budget hits 0, session throws `RetryBudgetExceeded` so app can surface fallback UI.

Marco: Go should mirror with explicit `Session` object that returns `ErrRetryBudgetExceeded` (typed) so callers can handle it explicitly.

DevBot: deploy-bot posted: "Canary deploy to staging for transport-resume changes at 18:00 UTC" :bell:

Alex: We should also document the resume token contract: tokens are opaque, short-lived (default 60s), and bound to a session id. They should not be relied on for long offline resumes; if customers need that, they should use paged APIs with server-side cursors.

Priya: Quick question: should resume tokens be emitted inline as fields on each chunk (so browsers can persist after any chunk) or only in metadata at chunk boundaries? Leaning inline labeled `resume_token` for ergonomics in browser clients.

Sara: Inline is nicer for browser JS where persisting after any chunk is common. Also helps flaky mobile networks.

Marco: One more item: default auto-batching heuristics. SDKs should pick batch size based on observed tail latency: if p99 < 50ms increase batch size gradually, else stay conservative. Expose `autoBatching: true|false` + `minBatch` / `maxBatch` knobs.

Alex: Action items: 1) Priya to draft minimal API shapes for `Session` + `RetryPolicy` for TS/Python/Go; 2) Marco to author the server resume-token spec + lifetime docs; 3) Sara to add dedupe guidance and examples to SDK docs; 4) Alex will prototype a TS `Session` POC this week.

Priya: I'll put a short RFC follow-up in the `docs` folder and tag `eng-platform`.

Marco: Sounds good, cc @Sara for dedupe heuristics and examples.

Sara: Ack — will sketch examples demonstrating client-side dedupe (stable ids and sequence numbers).

Alex: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD I'll merge the RFC follow-up and open small PRs mapping shape to each repo.
